text:
maria (sec): audit-bot flagged unusual high-volume GETs from `deploy-bot` to `customer-prod-s3` at ~00:03 UTC. Possible permission drift or cross-account assumeRole. https://logs.redwood/alerts/1895123456 :eyes:

audit-bot: ALERT ─ anomalous access pattern detected for service account `deploy-bot` (50 GETs, 78MB, 00:03-00:09 UTC). Severity: high. Ticket INC-2026-0456 created.

jonathan (sre): pausing `deploy-bot` tokens now. running: `authzctl revoke-token deploy-bot` :rotating_light:

lee (platform): I just applied an inline deny for s3:GetObject to `role/deploy-bot-service`. Pushing a quick policy patch to block read until we triage.
```
-        "Action": "s3:GetObject",
-        "Effect": "Allow",
+        "Action": "s3:GetObject",
+        "Effect": "Deny",
         "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::customer-prod-s3/*",
         "Principal": { "AWS": "arn:aws:iam::111111111:role/deploy-bot-service" }
```

anya (prod-sec): Can we confirm whether those objects contain PII? I see keys hit: `customers/12345/export.csv`, `customers/98765/profile.tar`. If PII, escalate to legal/compliance.

maria (sec): confirmed — 3 GETs for `customers/*` between 00:03 and 00:09. Files contain hashed+plain emails and phone columns. Marking as potential data exposure.

kevin (sec-analyst): querying STS logs for cross-account assumes. Hang on.
kevin (sec-analyst): found `sts:AssumeRole` at 00:02 from `arn:aws:iam::111111111:role/deploy-bot-service` -> `arn:aws:iam::222222222:role/analytics-read`. Looks like a cross-account trust allowed it to access analytics account S3 which proxies data.

lee (platform): that explains lateral access. I'm removing the `AssumeRole` statement from deploy-bot's policy and revoking the external trust on analytics account. Patch shown below (removing statement id `AllowAssumeAnalytics`).
```
-  "Statement": [
-    {
-      "Sid": "AllowAssumeAnalytics",
-      "Effect": "Allow",
-      "Action": "sts:AssumeRole",
-      "Resource": "arn:aws:iam::222222222:role/analytics-read"
-    },
-    ...
-  ]
+  "Statement": [
+    ... (AllowAssumeAnalytics removed) ...
+  ]
```

maria (sec): good. Next: rotate KMS key for bucket `customer-prod-s3`. Current key `kms-prod-01` was used in cross-account access. Any objections? :lock:

anya (prod-sec): rotate yes, but coordinate with backups and data pipelines. Create new key `kms-prod-02`, re-encrypt objects on a rolling window. I'll notify compliance and legal.

jonathan (sre): immediate mitigations I'm applying: 1) revoke `deploy-bot` tokens 2) deny s3:GetObject at role-level 3) remove cross-account trust 4) increase audit retention to 1y and export last 90 days to secure bucket. Commands: 
```
authzctl revoke-token deploy-bot
iamctl put-role-policy deploy-bot-service deny-s3-read.json
iamctl remove-role-trust analytics-account AllowAssumeAnalytics
logsctl export --query "arn:aws:iam::111111111:role/deploy-bot-service" --days 90 --dest s3://security-archive/inc-2026-0456
```

lee (platform): opened PR to remove assumeRole and tighten least-priv rules: https://git.redwood/infra/pulls/8421  — also adding automated CI check to detect inline cross-account sts statements for service accounts.

kevin (sec-analyst): running full list of principals that had access to analytics-read role in last 30d. Will attach results to the ticket.

maria (sec): owners for post-incident: maria (sec) — overall, lee (platform) — policy fixes/PR, kevin (sec-analyst) — audit & scope, anya (prod-sec) — compliance/legal contact. Postmortem to include timeline, root cause (cross-account trust + permissive service-account policy), remediation (KMS rotation, policy hardening), and follow-ups: 1) automated drift detection for service-account RBAC, 2) deny-by-default templates for service roles, 3) require approval for sts:AssumeRole to external accounts. :memo: :thumbsup:

audit-bot: Incident INC-2026-0456 updated to state "mitigations applied; investigation ongoing".

maria (sec): thanks team. keep updates in the ticket and ping here if anything else pops. :eyes:
